question.text:
2
For how many real values of k does (k − 1)x + 2kx + k + 1 = 0 have exactly one distinct real
solution?
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) Infinitely many

solution.text:
2
For k ̸= 1 the discriminant is 4k − 4(k − 1)(k + 1) = 4, so there are two distinct real roots.
At k = 1 the equation becomes 2x + 2 = 0, which has exactly one solution. Thus there is one
such parameter value.
